blogs.title: Intrinsic or Propensity? The Eighth Circuit's Prior Possession Doctrine in Felon-in-Possession Cases
blogs.description: This post examines the court's treatment of prior possession evidence under Rule 404(b), analyzing the distinction between intrinsic evidence and propensity evidence. The decision reinforces the Eighth Circuit's position that testimony about a defendant's prior possession of the same firearm is admissible as intrinsic evidence directly relevant to proving ownership or control—an issue that divides circuits and implicates the proper boundaries of the 'prior bad acts' prohibition.

blogs.title: No Charge Required: Section 2K2.1(b)(6)(B) and Sentencing Based on Uncharged Felony Conduct
blogs.description: This post analyzes the sentencing enhancement for possessing a firearm 'in connection with another felony offense,' focusing on Application Note 14(C)'s explicit allowance for enhancement even where no criminal charge was brought. The decision illustrates how uncharged conduct—here, kidnapping and assault—can substantially increase a guidelines range, raising questions about the relationship between charging discretion, jury fact-finding, and sentencing severity under the Guidelines.

blogs.title: Presumed Reasonable: The Eighth Circuit's Deferential Approach to Within-Guidelines ACCA Sentences
blogs.description: This post explores the interaction between Armed Career Criminal Act mandatory minimums and the advisory guidelines, particularly where multiple sentencing enhancements produce overlapping calculations. The decision highlights how courts handle defendants' arguments that guidelines enhancements conflict with § 3553(a)'s parsimony principle, and the strong presumption of reasonableness that attaches to within-range sentences in the Eighth Circuit.
